title: Agent::in_transaction commits twice for every transaction
description:
Agent::in_transaction opens with self.save() before BEGIN IMMEDIATE:

    // What was delivered before is saved on its own first.
    self.save()?;

crate::state::save UPDATEs the agent_state row unconditionally, so that
pre-save always dirties a page and, with nothing else holding a
transaction, is a committed write transaction of its own. Every
in_transaction call therefore costs two commits, not one, and
in_transaction is how the agent builds every Commit, handles every
server Message and ends every outbox entry.

Measured on the first-private-message path, after bead mimid-604m.6
batched Agent::host_room: host_room commits 4 times, of which 2 are the
one transaction and its pre-save, 1 is the save after Room/create and 1
is publishing this device's first KeyPackage.

## Why it is not just removable

The pre-save is what makes a rollback safe to be coarse. Agent::roll_back
reads the state back from the database and reloads the groups, discarding
whatever the in-memory state held; the pre-save is what puts the
already-delivered journal entries, and any state change made before the
call, where the rollback can find them. Skipping it when
self.undelivered is empty would still drop in-memory state changes made
before the call, and the set of callers that have one is not obvious from
the call sites.

So this is a durability question about what a rollback is allowed to
lose, not a refactor: for Mark. If the answer is that in_transaction may
keep the pre-save only when there is something to save, every agent write
costs one commit instead of two.
